notes: High-signal mid-market account. Evaluated Redwood Hosted API first for fast integration; now pushing toward Dedicated because of predictable latency and data isolation. Key ask: run a 6-week Dedicated POC to validate canary + fallback routing. POC asks: canary at 5% traffic in prod-like staging, metrics-driven promotion, fallback route to hosted_api model variant in eu-west-1 if p95 latency > 500ms or error-rate spike > 1%. Model plan: start with Redwood-verified Llama-2-Chat-13B quantized variant for quality baseline, have a smaller 7B quantized variant as low-cost fallback. "Rollback" plan required: automated traffic cutover back to hosted API + immediate alert + postmortem. Customer quoted: "need no surprises on cost spikes — show us a predictable unit cost and burst caps". Latency targets in POC: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for single-turn chat on 1k token context; throughput target ~120 reqs/min sustained with autoscale test to 400 rpm burst. Important constraints: VPC peering required, KMS customer-managed key, SOC2 + audit logs retention 1 year, EU data residency for subset of EU customers. Procurement is price-sensitive; wants committed reserved pool pricing vs pay-as-you-go. SE notes: KV prefix caching + intelligent batching may reduce cost by ~18% on their workload (based on sample traces). Actionable next steps: produce SOW for Dedicated POC (scope, success metrics, rollback criteria), provide cost model for 3 scenarios (steady, peak, canary), schedule procurement handoff. Short-hand: "POC scope agreed; need SOW + procurement sign-off; network + KMS gating items."
technical_summary: Will validate routing policies: 1) Canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) using feature flags; 2) Fallback routing to hosted_api or smaller model variant on SLA breach; 3) Region failover: primary us-east-1, secondary eu-west-1 for EU traffic with automated DNS failover and capacity check; 4) Rollback: immediate traffic cut to hosted_api + preserves in-flight KV cache; monitoring hooks to Console (per-route latency, token counts, error traces).
billing_notes: Customer prefers monthly reserved commit for Dedicated. Asked for three pricing bands: 1) minimal (base reserved), 2) expected (base + 30% buffer), 3) peak (with burst add-on). Wants per-route token-level visibility and alerting on monthly burn > 110% forecast.
